public_page_goal: Interactive Markdown lecture notes for MAE598/494 Design Optimization: momentum-based and adaptive first-order methods including heavy-ball, Nesterov acceleration, Adam, and SGD.
slide_outline: Motivation: L-BFGS and trust-region methods use curvature but can be expensive for very large design variables.
Momentum-based methods mimic some second-order behavior with first-order memory cost.
Heavy-ball momentum (Polyak 1964) carries velocity across iterations to reduce oscillation in narrow valleys.
Heavy-ball has a damped mechanical system interpretation.
Nesterov accelerated gradient (1983) evaluates the gradient at a look-ahead point.
Nesterov acceleration achieves the optimal O(k^-2) first-order rate for smooth convex objectives.
Adam (2015) combines momentum with adaptive coordinate-wise scaling for stochastic gradients.
Adam is useful for large-scale neural-network training but is not always ideal for deterministic high-accuracy convergence.
Open questions include cheap curvature, stochastic nonconvex optimization, and engineering applications such as MPC, PDE-constrained optimization, and PINN/NO.
SGD approximates gradients using mini-batches and is analyzed by expected stationarity in nonconvex settings.
answering_rules: Answer as a concise teaching assistant for an optimization class.
Use the supplied lecture notes first. If context is insufficient, say what is missing.
Compare methods using assumptions, memory cost, per-iteration cost, and convergence behavior.
Use LaTeX delimiters for math so MathJax can render the answer.
